title: Anime Recommender - overview
description: Start here. Reads top to bottom: is the product working, what is it serving, where does the time go, what does it cost, which model answered, and is anything underneath broken. Deep dives: 'LLM and venue routing' and 'Infrastructure'.

panels.title: 1 - Is the product working right now?
Requests / sec
panels.description: Served HTTP requests across all routes. The denominator for every rate below — a quiet dashboard usually means no traffic, not no problems.

panels.title: 5xx error rate
panels.description: Share of requests that failed outright. Degraded answers are NOT counted here: the system returns 200 with a notice when it falls back, by design, so this is only real breakage.

panels.title: p95 /v1/recommend
panels.description: 95th percentile end-to-end latency of the main endpoint, including retrieval, rerank and the LLM call.

panels.title: Cache hit rate
panels.description: Share of recommend requests answered from the response cache. Every hit skips an embed, a retrieval round trip and an LLM call, so this line is most of the cost story.

panels.title: LLM spend (window)
panels.description: Metered spend over the selected time range. Only priced models count — see 'Unpriced LLM calls' for the leak.

panels.title: Refusals / sec
panels.description: The model declining honestly (out of scope, or nothing matched). Healthy behaviour — but a SPIKE means either an abuse wave or a retrieval regression starving the model of candidates.

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: Traffic split across endpoints. A route that disappears here is a client that stopped calling, not necessarily a failure.

panels.title: Responses by status class
panels.description: 2xx/4xx/5xx over time. 4xx rising alone is usually auth or validation (including 429s); 5xx is ours.

panels.title: Answers vs refusals
panels.description: What users actually received. A refusal is a 200 with no recommendations, so it is invisible in the status-code chart above.

panels.title: Quota rejections by scope
panels.description: Requests refused by a quota (the 429 path). Steadily rising = the free-tier cap has become the product's ceiling, which is a pricing decision, not an incident.

panels.title: /v1/recommend latency percentiles
panels.description: p50 is the typical user; p95/p99 are the ones who leave. A p99 far above p95 means a tail problem (cold model, slow dependency), not a general slowdown.

panels.title: Retrieval stage p95
panels.description: Which stage owns the latency: embed, dense (pgvector), sparse (FTS), rerank (cross-encoder), mmr. 'The request took 5s' is not actionable; 'rerank took 4.8s of it' is.

panels.title: Stage failures and timeouts
panels.description: Stages that did not finish. These are SILENT: retrieval degrades on purpose, so the request still returns 200 while quietly getting worse. A rerank timeout also disables venue routing entirely.

panels.title: LLM latency p95 by model
panels.description: Time inside each model's call, measured at the shared provider seam. This replaces a by-host breakdown of outbound HTTP: the OTel client instrumentation on this stack emits no peer label, so every provider's calls landed in one undifferentiated series and the panel could never answer 'is it us or them'. Per-provider detail is in the collapsible sections below.

panels.title: LLM cost rate (USD/hour) by model
panels.description: Spend extrapolated to an hourly rate, per model. The self-hosted venue meters at $0, so a drop here with steady traffic means routing sent work to the GPU.

panels.title: Tokens/sec by model and direction
panels.description: Input vs output tokens. Output is the expensive half almost everywhere, and it is what the venue's throughput has to keep up with.

panels.title: Unpriced LLM calls
panels.description: Calls the provider billed but we metered at $0 because the model is missing from LLM_PRICING. Any non-zero value means cost is leaking unattributed - alert on it.

panels.title: Routing decisions / sec
panels.description: hosted = confidence below threshold (the normal majority) - venue_served = the self-hosted GPU answered - venue_fallback_error / _empty = the venue was tried and could not deliver.

panels.title: Venue share of answers
panels.description: Percentage of routed answers served by the self-hosted engine. Zero with a healthy engine is not a bug: it means retrieval confidence never cleared the threshold. See the LLM deep-dive.

panels.title: vLLM - calls / sec
panels.description: Requests this provider answered. Zero means routing never chose it — which for the venue rows is the normal case when retrieval confidence sits below the threshold. Both self-hosted engines serve the SAME model name, so these app-level panels cannot tell vLLM from SGLang; the engine panels in this row can.

panels.title: vLLM - request p95
panels.description: 95th percentile of the full call, measured at the one seam every provider passes through. Both self-hosted engines serve the SAME model name, so these app-level panels cannot tell vLLM from SGLang; the engine panels in this row can.

panels.title: vLLM - TTFT p50
panels.description: Median time to first streamed token: what a user feels as 'did it hear me'. Streaming requests only — a non-streaming call cannot measure it. Both self-hosted engines serve the SAME model name, so these app-level panels cannot tell vLLM from SGLang; the engine panels in this row can.

panels.title: vLLM - TTFT p95
panels.description: Tail time to first token. Both self-hosted engines serve the SAME model name, so these app-level panels cannot tell vLLM from SGLang; the engine panels in this row can.

panels.title: vLLM - cost / request
panels.description: Metered spend divided by calls over 30m. The self-hosted venue meters at $0 by construction, which is the whole economic argument for routing to it. Both self-hosted engines serve the SAME model name, so these app-level panels cannot tell vLLM from SGLang; the engine panels in this row can.

panels.title: vLLM - error rate
panels.description: Share of this provider's calls that failed and fell through to the next tier. A provider can be 'up' and still be failing every structured-output parse. Both self-hosted engines serve the SAME model name, so these app-level panels cannot tell vLLM from SGLang; the engine panels in this row can.

panels.title: vLLM - latency percentiles
panels.description: p50/p95/p99 for this provider alone. Comparing these rows against each other is how you judge whether routing to the GPU actually pays off. Both self-hosted engines serve the SAME model name, so these app-level panels cannot tell vLLM from SGLang; the engine panels in this row can.

panels.title: vLLM - tokens / sec
panels.description: Input vs output tokens for this provider. Output is the expensive half almost everywhere, and it is what the venue's decode rate has to keep up with. Both self-hosted engines serve the SAME model name, so these app-level panels cannot tell vLLM from SGLang; the engine panels in this row can.

panels.title: vLLM - engine up
panels.description: 1 = vLLM is running and scrapeable. 0 is normal in API-LLM mode (make up) and whenever SGLang holds the GPU instead — only one engine can.

panels.title: vLLM - requests running
panels.description: Sequences the engine is decoding right now.

panels.title: vLLM - requests waiting
panels.description: Queued behind the running batch. Sustained non-zero means the GPU is the bottleneck, not the app.

panels.title: vLLM - KV cache used
panels.description: Share of the paged KV cache in use. Near 100% and new requests queue; this is what --gpu-memory-utilization actually buys.

panels.title: vLLM - engine TTFT p95
panels.description: Time to first token as the ENGINE measures it, excluding network and app overhead. The gap against the app-level TTFT above is what the round trip costs.

panels.title: vLLM - engine TPOT p95
panels.description: Time per output token after the first — the decode rate a reader experiences as speed.

panels.title: vLLM - engine throughput
panels.description: Prompt tokens are prefill work; generation tokens are decode work. Prefill spikes with long contexts, decode scales with answer length.

panels.title: vLLM - queue vs end-to-end (p95)
panels.description: Queue time separates 'the model is slow' from 'the model is busy'. If queue dominates, add capacity or shed load.

panels.title: vLLM - prefix cache hit rate
panels.description: Reused KV blocks across requests. A shared system prompt should keep this high; near zero means every request pays full prefill.

panels.title: SGLang - engine up
panels.description: 1 = SGLang is running and scrapeable. This row and the vLLM row are mutually exclusive by design: one GPU, one engine (make up-sglang / make up-vllm).

panels.title: SGLang - running requests
panels.description: Requests the engine is decoding now.

panels.title: SGLang - queued requests
panels.description: Requests waiting for a slot.

panels.title: SGLang - token pool used
panels.description: KV token-pool utilisation. SGLang's --mem-fraction-static is a share of TOTAL VRAM, not of what is free, which is why a fraction that works on an idle card can starve the cache on a busy desktop (measured here: 0.50 gave a 1,618-token cache, 0.70 gave 42,669).

panels.title: SGLang - engine TTFT p95
panels.description: Time to first token measured inside the engine.

panels.title: SGLang - cache hit rate
panels.description: RadixAttention prefix reuse across requests.

panels.title: SGLang - engine throughput
panels.description: Prefill and decode token rates reported by SGLang. These series exist only while SGLang is the running engine; the panel is empty under vLLM, which is information, not a fault.

panels.title: Groq - calls / sec
panels.description: Requests this provider answered. Zero means routing never chose it — which for the venue rows is the normal case when retrieval confidence sits below the threshold. Matched by model name (gpt-oss, llama, mixtral, gemma). This is the tier the app calls whenever retrieval confidence sits below the routing threshold, so in normal operation it carries most traffic.

panels.title: Circuit breaker transitions
panels.description: A breaker opening is a dependency that started failing; open -> half_open -> open repeating means it never recovered and the fallback has been carrying the product.

panels.title: Scrape targets up (1 = healthy)
panels.description: Every monitored component. A venue-engine at 0 is expected in API-LLM mode; anything else at 0 means that component is down or unreachable.
